nodes.description: The hormonal state that drives the entry, recorded as an exposure record with the direction reversed, following the convention design decisions section 19 sets for a menopause fact of this kind: bind the hormonal state rather than the life stage, because ECTO has no menopause term and the stage is not an exposure. The same record covers iatrogenic withdrawal - bilateral oophorectomy, gonadotoxic chemotherapy, pelvic radiation, and the aromatase inhibitors and gonadotropin-releasing hormone agonists used in breast cancer treatment, in which the syndrome is a recognised and often severe consequence.

nodes.description: Dehydroepiandrosterone delivered as a 0.50% (6.5 mg) intravaginal insert once daily, approved for moderate to severe dyspareunia due to menopause. Its mechanism is intracrine rather than endocrine: the vaginal tissue converts the inactive precursor locally into androgens and estrogens, and in the phase 3 trial serum steroid levels stayed within the normal postmenopausal range while the local endpoints all moved, so the drug supplies the withdrawn ligand to the target tissue without restoring it systemically. It is the one treatment curated here that engages the androgen arm the consensus definition names beside estrogen. In the trial, 482 women over 12 weeks, it moved the same four coprimary endpoints as ospemifene plus the gynaecological assessment of secretions, epithelial integrity, surface thickness and colour. Its pooled symptom estimate in the class-level network meta-analysis spans the null, so it sits beside ospemifene as an alternative to local estrogen rather than ahead of it, and endometrial safety beyond one year has not been studied.

nodes.description: The module's tissue-agnostic receptor node, instantiated in the urogenital tract. The substitution the primer asks for is made here: the responsive populations are the stratified squamous epithelium of the vagina and vestibule and the transitional epithelium of the urethra and bladder trigone, together with the subepithelial stroma and vasculature they sit on. Both receptor paralogues are present in human vaginal tissue and both are expressed at their highest level before menopause, so the lost signal is not attributable to one isoform; in mouse urogenital tissue the alpha transcript is concentrated in the vagina rather than in the upper urinary tract, which is consistent with the vaginal lesion being the more severe of the two. The receptors themselves are intact, so the activity is reduced rather than absent.

nodes.description: Lactobacilli ferment glycogen-derived sugars to lactic acid and hold the premenopausal vaginal lumen below pH 4.5; as the substrate is withdrawn the community thins and the pH rises into the high fours and above. This is the node with the weakest internal evidence in the entry and the description says so rather than overstating it: in the cited cohort both the lactobacillus difference and the pH difference between premenopausal and postmenopausal women were trends that did not reach significance, and some postmenopausal women retained substantial glycogen and lactobacilli. What does hold is the pH half from the opposite direction, since local estradiol significantly lowers vaginal pH in a placebo-controlled trial. The node is kept because it is the step that connects the epithelial lesion to the recurrent urinary tract infection phenotype, and because its reversal is a measured treatment effect. Contrast with bacterial vaginosis, which reaches a similar luminal state by a different route - the lactobacilli are displaced by anaerobes rather than starved of substrate - and which is this entry's main differential.

nodes.description: Over-the-counter water-, silicone- or hyaluronic-acid-based preparations, applied on a schedule as a moisturizer or before intercourse as a lubricant. The North American Menopause Society puts them first for mild symptoms, where non-prescription therapy is held to relieve most women, and reserves the hormonal and SERM options for moderate to severe disease. They are the only treatment curated here that does not act on the lesion: in a randomised three-arm comparison against vaginal estrogen and radiofrequency, the moisturizer arm moved none of the three objective markers - vaginal health index, vaginal maturation and pH - while all three arms improved symptomatically, so the preparation substitutes for the lubrication the atrophic tissue no longer makes rather than restoring the tissue. The efficacy evidence is weak in both directions: the class-level network meta-analysis puts its pooled symptom estimate at 0.15 with an interval spanning no effect, and a three-arm randomised trial found neither a moisturizer nor a vaginal estradiol tablet better than a placebo vaginal tablet plus gel.

nodes.description: An oral selective estrogen receptor modulator, 60 mg once daily, approved for moderate to severe dyspareunia due to menopause. It is the only approved SERM with a near-full estrogen agonist effect on the vaginal epithelium while remaining neutral to slightly estrogenic in the endometrium, which is what makes a systemically administered drug usable for a local indication. It was the first non-hormonal treatment approved for that indication. In its pivotal phase 3 trial, 605 women randomised against placebo for 12 weeks, it moved all four coprimary endpoints: parabasal cells down, superficial cells up, vaginal pH down and dyspareunia severity down. It is a second-line option rather than a competitor to local estrogen - the North American Menopause Society lists it among the treatments for moderate to severe disease and not for mild disease, and in the class-level network meta-analysis its pooled symptom estimate spans the null. Hot flushes are its characteristic adverse effect, which is the predictable cost of a systemic SERM in this population, and endometrial safety beyond one year has not been studied.

nodes.description: Estrogen withdrawal reduces the subepithelial vascular supply and with it the transudate and secretion that lubricate the vagina and vestibule. The node is kept distinct from the epithelial nodes above because it produces dryness and dyspareunia by a different route and because only the epithelial lesion is tracked by the maturation index.

nodes.description: Circulating estradiol falls to a postmenopausal range and stays there. The node is the systemic hormonal state and is the entry's root: it is the same fall whichever urogenital tissue is being considered, and it is entered by the same routes the module describes - follicle-pool exhaustion in natural menopause, bilateral oophorectomy, or gonadotoxic chemotherapy or pelvic radiation. Androgen withdrawal accompanies it and the consensus definition names "estrogen and other sex steroids" rather than estrogen alone, which matters for the two tissues (vestibule, periurethral stroma) where androgen receptor density is high; this entry does not separate the two hormones into distinct nodes because no cited source attributes a specific urogenital lesion to the androgen arm on its own.

nodes.description: The urethral and trigonal transitional epithelium shares the urogenital sinus origin and the estrogen receptor of the vaginal epithelium and atrophies with it, which is the structural basis of the syndrome's urinary arm. The measurable index is urethral maturation, the urethral counterpart of the vaginal maturation index, and local estradiol raises it within four weeks. Whether that structural change translates into symptom relief is a separate question and the cited trial answers it only partly: its primary storage-symptom endpoint was negative at twelve weeks while urgency incontinence improved at both time points, so this node is better supported structurally than symptomatically.

nodes.description: The vaginal and vestibular epithelium loses proliferative drive and thins from many layers of superficial and intermediate cells to a few layers of parabasal cells. The measurable index is the maturation index, the proportion of parabasal to superficial cells on a vaginal smear, and the node is established from the treatment side: three randomised trials of three different drug classes - local estrogen, the oral selective estrogen receptor modulator ospemifene, and intravaginal prasterone - each move parabasal cells down and superficial cells up against placebo or against a non-hormonal comparator, so the parabasal predominance of the untreated postmenopausal epithelium depends on signalling through the estrogen receptor. This node is curated apart from the glycogen node beside it rather than bundled with it, because the two feed different downstream arms - this one the dryness, burning and itching symptoms, the other the microbial chain - and because no source cited here measures both. The one source that discusses both states that whether luminal glycogen tracks epithelial glycogen deposits is an open question, so no edge is drawn between the two nodes either.

nodes.description: The epithelium stops delivering glycogen into the vaginal lumen, withdrawing the carbon source the luminal lactobacilli depend on. The claim is specifically about free glycogen in genital fluid rather than intraepithelial staining, because that is the fraction the cited study measured and the fraction available to the lumen: the same study records that significant glycogen staining has been seen in smears from postmenopausal and ovariectomized women and that intraepithelial glycogen has been reported to be independent of hormonal change, so the node does not claim the epithelium stops making glycogen altogether. That is also why it is a sibling of the epithelial atrophy node above rather than its consequence: the same study names the relationship between luminal glycogen and epithelial glycogen deposits as a critical open question, so an edge from thinning to glycogen loss would assert what the source declines to establish.

nodes.description: Estrogen governs collagen turnover in the vaginal and periurethral wall, and its withdrawal leaves that turnover unregulated, with loss of elasticity, narrowing and shortening of the vagina and reduced distensibility of the introitus. The direction of the collagen effect is not the simple one: in the cited placebo-controlled trial six months of estradiol decreased total collagen while raising matrix metalloproteinase-2 expression and immature cross-links, which the authors read as accelerated turnover - aged collagen degraded and new collagen laid down - rather than net accumulation. This node therefore asserts loss of regulated turnover, not simply loss of collagen, and the entry does not claim that postmenopausal vaginal collagen content is lower than premenopausal.

biological_processes: estrogen-regulated collagen turnover in the vaginal and periurethral wall

nodes.description: Itching of the vulva, listed by the Cochrane review beside dryness, discomfort and painful intercourse among the symptoms of vaginal atrophy, and one of the five qualifying symptoms a randomised trial of local therapy enrolled on. Recorded separately from the burning and irritation phenotype above because itching is a different sensation with a different ontology outcome: HP:0032004 was rejected there as a stand-in for burning, which is a different claim, and it is the exact term for this one. Searching HP for "pruritus" (OLS, 2026-11-14) returns 19 terms, of which two are specific to this region - HP:0032004 Pruritus vulvae, "A sensation of itching in the vulvar region", and HP:0030161 Vaginal pruritus, "A sensation of itching in the vagina" - and they are sibling children of HP:0000989 Pruritus rather than a general and a specific form of one thing, with no combined vulvovaginal term between them. The cited sources report the symptom as vulvovaginal, so this row's claim is narrowed to the vulva to match its binding rather than the binding widened to cover a site the term does not name. No second row is curated for the vaginal half: neither source distinguishes the two sites, so splitting one reported symptom across two phenotypes would assert a distinction the sources do not make.

evidence.reference_title: Local oestrogen for vaginal atrophy in postmenopausal women.
evidence.snippet: Vaginal atrophy is a frequent complaint of postmenopausal women; symptoms include vaginal dryness, itching, discomfort and painful intercourse.

evidence.reference_title: Efficacy of Vaginal Estradiol or Vaginal Moisturizer vs Placebo for Treating Postmenopausal Vulvovaginal Symptoms: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
evidence.snippet: This 12-week multicenter randomized clinical trial enrolled postmenopausal women with moderate to severe symptoms of vulvovaginal itching, pain, dryness, irritation, or pain with penetration.

nodes.description: Burning and irritation of the vulva and vagina, named in the consensus definition alongside dryness and deliberately left unbound, because HPO has no term for it. Searched OLS on 2026-11-14. HP "vulvar" returns 17 terms: six neoplastic, plus vulvar abscess, vulvodynia, pruritus vulvae, abnormal vulvar morphology, three labial terms, Bartholin cyst, persistent HPV infection and recurrent bacterial vaginosis. HP "burning" returns 65 terms including site-specific ones for other sites - HP:0032143 Burning mouth and HP:6000420 Burning eye sensation - and none for the vulva or vagina. HP "irritation" returns irritability and site-specific inflammations only. The nearest candidates are therefore HP:0030943 Vulvodynia, defined as "Pain in the vulvar area", and HP:0032004 Pruritus vulvae, "A sensation of itching in the vulvar region". Binding Vulvodynia would assert a distinct chronic idiopathic vulvar pain entity, and Pruritus vulvae would substitute itching for burning, so the phenotype carries a free-text preferred term and no binding. HPO's existing Burning mouth and Burning eye sensation terms are the pattern a term request for this one would follow. Itching, which the same sources list beside burning, is a separate claim and is carried as the Vulvar Pruritus phenotype below, where HP:0032004 fits it exactly; this phenotype is the burning and irritation half, which stays unbound.

evidence.reference_title: Genitourinary syndrome of menopause: new terminology for vulvovaginal atrophy from the International Society for the Study of Women's Sexual Health and the North American Menopause Society.
evidence.snippet: The syndrome may include but is not limited to genital symptoms of dryness, burning, and irritation; sexual symptoms of lack of lubrication, discomfort or pain, and impaired function; and urinary symptoms of urgency, dysuria and recurrent urinary tract infections.
